The ability to effectively access the literature in diverse fields within Life Sciences is essential for the ability to pursue research projects in whatever direction they may lead.
First-year ILS graduate students will be introduced to the primary research literature through the in-depth analysis of papers selected from across the breadth of the ILS program.

objectives: Students will gain hands-on experience in a professional field in organizational settings, such as higher education, industry, government, or the non-profit sector.
Students will work in settings that demonstrate the ways in which graduate training can be applied to meet the needs of the host organization.
Students will participate in structured mentoring activities that broaden exposure to potential career paths in the host organization beyond the scope of the intern’s immediate work duties.
Students will integrate new professional experiences into their educational program through reflective activities.
Students will consider meaningful insights for future growth as highlighted by the internship experience.
Students will broaden their professional networks to include individuals in career paths beyond traditional academic roles.

Students will provide a written report at the end of the internship experience detailing:
Progress towards objectives in the learning contract;
Impact of the internship experience on career planning/goals; and
Anticipated next steps towards their career goals.
